reviews.reason: The named owner and extracted child/controller boundaries below explain this component; declaration length alone is not a demonstrated competing responsibility or behavior failure. RoleDataPolicySection has real editable default/model-policy drafts but synchronizes them from each query data change without a dirty or role-owner guard. The role query is keyed by roleCode while local draft survives prop changes; replaceSettingsRoleDataPolicy uses the current roleCode with those retained values. Parent save only checks edit permission, not query readiness/owner. Table loading overlay is not a submission guard.

The components are cohesive private provider/consumer or explicitly separate scene fixtures; no shared state/lifecycle defect is identified. SortablePolicyTable keeps sortable row, drag handle and table together because they share the private row-handle context and DndContext provider contract. These are cohesive cooperating components, not unrelated exports. useContext is supported in React 19.

The displayed source uses two linear semantic stages (select valid/authorized items, then project payload/UI) with no repeated expensive effect; original ordering and identity are intentional. policyTableRows filters catalogGroups by kind and only then assigns display_key to the filtered display order. SortablePolicyTable uses this display order; combining passes with the original catalog index would change drag/reorder positions. It is a linear projection, not repeated expensive lookup.
